full_judgment:
26. The law relating to the burden of proof is stated in section 101 of the Evidence Act which runs thus: 

 When a person is bound to prove the existence of any fact, it is said that the burden of proof lies on that person." 

 27. The burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. Moreover, it is but reasonable and just that the suitor who relies upon the existence of a fact, shoula be called upon to prove his own case. The party on whom the onus of proof lies must in order to succeed, establish a prima facie case. He cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof. The burden of proving his case is upon the claimant. Here in this case both sides have two different cases and they have to prove their respective case. 

 29. The first allegation of the petitioner is that the alleged will was created antedated by forgery after the death of Mokshada Bala Dasaya. PW 1 Shishubala Roy deposed that Mokshada Bala Dasaya did not execute the will and the same is forged one. When this allegation is supported by oral evidence, then the burden of proof shifts to the opposite party vide rulings reported in the case of Pannu Geegania vs Devi Proshad AIR 1963 MP 15. But the opposite party has totally failed to adduce any evidence in this respect. 

 44. Scanning both the oral and documentary evidence, we find that the learned District Judge erred both in law and fact in ignoring the documentary evidence, Exhibit 1 and the oral evidence of PWs. 1 to 4 and relying only on Exhibit Ka a registered deed dated 9-5-78 produced by the respondent No. 1 showing that the name of the father Fakuram Hazra is Gopal Ram Hazra, which is not a conclusive proof in itself, and it having been rebutted by the oral evidence of PWs 1 to 4 and documentary evidence Exhibit 1. PWs 1, 2 and 3 and 4 proved the fact that Dhaneshwar, Fakuram and Laba Krishna are full brothers and their evidence having been fortified by, the Power of Attorney Exhibit 1 executed by PW 2 Nani Gopal Hazra in favour of his sister PW 1 Shishubala who are son and daughter of late Dhaneshwar nevertheless, the learned District Judge erred both in law and fact in not holding that the appellant has proved the proceedings both by oral and documentary evidence.
